title: land's rebase resolves a conflict confined to the landing item's own file by merging its keys
goal: when backlog.py land's rebase of work/<id> stops only on the landing item's own item file, land merges the two sides key by key (gates and notes from both, a scalar both sides changed alike kept, a scalar changed differently left as a conflict) and goes on, instead of stopping at step rebase for a hand rebase
notes: SP-yjfiemha retrospective, 2026-10-19: land BG-jemfbkjs stopped at step rebase (ops land.step rebase exit=1): the orchestrator's main-branch commit reworded the item's title and notes while the worker's fix commit added its gate g1 to the same file; the orchestrator re-made the worktree, kept both sides (gates plus the longer notes) and landed on the second run. Check is a placeholder: at planning, plant the two conflicting commits on a fixture and drive land. A lighter alternative: a rule that the orchestrator rewords a landing item only on its branch.
